newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Trade on South Africa's bond market was marked by good two-way dealing on Wednesday after the market got off to a strong start on the back sharp gains in U.S. long bonds overnight.
The key R150 stock was at 15.14 pct around 1400 GMT from 15.20 percent late on Tueday. It reached an intraday best level of 15.09 pct during the morning on good institutional and offshore demand.
"Players were keen to go long at current levels and we saw some good two-way trade," one bond trader said.
But the U.S. long bond market's retracement in early New York trade pulled the local market of its stronger levels.
The yield on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond moved to 7.13 percent after settling at 7.10 percent on Tuesday night in the wake of stronger-than-expected March U.S. industrial production data.
U.S. indutrial output grew 0.9 percent against a forecast 0.6 percent, while capacity utilisation came in at 84.1 percent against an expected 83.6 percent.
"The market weakened on the U.S. but nothing major...I'm expecting a stronger trend tommorrow based on good interest today with 15 percent a key level to break on the downside," a second trader said.
Foreigners bought 494.27 million rand's worth of South African stock on Tuesday after buying 288.24 million rand on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 4.54 billion rand on Tuesday from 3.34 billion rand on Monday, it said.
The rand ended around the day's weakest levels against the U.S dollar but little changed on the day after consistent importer demand during the afternoon.
Forex traders said the unit had put in a remarkeably steady performance during the week given the U.S. dollar's recent resurgence.
"We've seen a sustained period of stability with some good interest from offshore and also on the local front," UAL Merchant Bank's Neal Anderson commented.
Others said there was good interest from across the shore to buy rands at the slightly higher levels.
"I'm expecting 4.4500 to 4.4650 to hold tommorrow with the underlying tone looking positive," a second forex trader said.
At 1415 GMT the rand was at 4.4575/4605 against an easier dollar from 4.4590/4620 overnight.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.1883/2253 yen from 28.3137/3552 yen, 0.3874/3879 marks from 0.3885/3889 marks and 7.2293/2386 rand against sterling from 7.2467/2547 rand.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates were quoted steady in a 16.60 to 16.65 percent offered range, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.95 and 16.10 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage fell to 8.411 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.283 billion rand on Monday, the Reserve Bank said.
